text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The conservative coalition partner won 10 districts out of 12 in local by-elections held on Sunday.
- President Suleyman Demirel's four day-long Germany visit begins on Monday. Demirel is expected to urge Germany to take firmer action against terrorism.
- An MP, organised crime boss and former police chief involved in mysterious car accident.
- Conservative main opposition says the government's success in local by-elections is down to them being in power and giving away money.
- Tourism minister takes a U-turn in banning Turkish citizens from casinos and says they will now be let in.
- Half of a 15-tonne consignment of diseased wheat from India is stolen from the warehouse.
- Transport ministry speeds up 11 projects worth around $12 billion for 1997.

- Islamist Welfare Party approves easing of freedom of expression laws in human right package conditional on changes on a ban on civil servants wearing the Islamic headscarve scarve and regulations in the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca.
- Foreign ships sailing through the Bosphorus straits with no pilot pose constant danger of accident and polution.
